true_answer: Also, explain why the answer is not 95. While we are thinking about sets, consider what happens to the addi- tive principle when the sets are NOT disjoint. Suppose we want to find | A ∪ B | and know that | A | | 10 and | B | | 8 . This is not enough informa- tion though. We do not know how many of the 8 elements in B are also elements of A . However, if we also know that | A ∩ B | | 6 , then we can say exactly how many elements are in A , and, of those, how many are in B and how many are not (6 of the 10 elements are in B , so 4 are in A but not in B ).
